lines.name: Higashiyama Line
lines.description: Nagoya's first subway (Nagoya - Sakae, 1957) and its busiest line.

lines.name: Meijō Line
lines.description: Loop line, completed in 2004 (Japan's first subway loop). Shiyakusho station was renamed Nagoyajō in 2023.

lines.name: Meikō Line
lines.description: Kanayama - Nagoyakō. Part of the Meijō Line until 2004; trains run through from the Meijō Line. Officially shares the Meijō purple; drawn in a darker purple to tell them apart.

lines.name: Tsurumai Line
lines.description: Through service with the Meitetsu Inuyama Line at Kami-Otai (1993) and the Meitetsu Toyota Line at Akaike (1979).

lines.name: Sakura-dōri Line
lines.description: Western terminus Nakamura-kuyakusho was renamed Taikō-dōri in 2023. The extensions shown as proposed come from the 1992 council report and are frozen (see research notes).

segments.label: West extension Taikō-dōri - Shippō (1992 report No. 12, frozen; approximate)
East extension Tokushige - Toyoake-kita (1992 report No. 12, frozen; approximate)

lines.name: Kamiiida Line
lines.description: 0.8 km link to the Meitetsu Komaki Line (through service). The extension south to Shinsakae-machi and Marutamachi (1992 report No. 12) is frozen; Nagoya City has no plan to build it (2024).

segments.label: Extension Heian-dōri - Marutamachi (1992 report No. 12, frozen; approximate)

lines.name: Tōkaidō Line
lines.description: Gamagōri - Nagoya - Gifu - Ōgaki - Tarui within the map area. Colour chosen for the map (JR Central uses one corporate orange).

lines.name: Tōkaidō Line (Mino-Akasaka branch)
lines.nameLocal: 東海道本線 美濃赤坂支線
lines.description: Ōgaki - Mino-Akasaka branch (3 stations, unnumbered).

lines.name: Chūō Line
lines.description: Nagoya - Tajimi (cut at Tajimi; the line continues to Nakatsugawa and Shiojiri). Colour chosen for the map.

lines.name: Kansai Line
lines.description: Nagoya - Kuwana (cut at Kuwana; continues to Kameyama). Colour chosen for the map.

lines.name: Taketoyo Line
lines.description: Ōbu - Taketoyo. Aichi's first railway (1886), built to carry materials for the Tōkaidō Line. Colour chosen for the map.

lines.name: Takayama Line
lines.description: Gifu - Mino-Ōta (cut at Mino-Ōta; continues to Takayama and Toyama). Colour chosen for the map.

lines.name: Taita Line
lines.description: Tajimi - Mino-Ōta. Colour chosen for the map.

lines.name: Tōkaidō Shinkansen
lines.description: Operated by JR Central. Mikawa-Anjō station opened in 1988. Clipped at the map area.

lines.name: Chūō Shinkansen (maglev)
lines.description: SCMaglev by JR Central; no official colour (chosen for the map). Shinagawa - Nagoya (285.6 km, construction plan approved 2014): the underground Nagoya station is being dug under JR Nagoya and the ~34 km Daiichi Chūkyōken Tunnel (Nagoya - Kasugai - Kani) is being bored; Gifu Prefecture station is at Nakatsugawa, east of the map area. No official opening year: JR Central's last formal statement (2024-03) is "2034 or later"; it said in 2026 a new date would be given within the year (press expects 2036 or later). Total cost ~¥11 trillion (2025-10). Nagoya - Shin-Osaka (~152 km, via Nara) is in the 2011 development plan, environmental assessment started 2023-12; route and Mie station (Kameyama, three candidate sites) not fixed; government target "2037 at the earliest". Paths are approximate.

segments.label: Nagoya - Gifu Prefecture station (part of Shinagawa - Nagoya; construction, opening "2034 or later")
Nagoya - Shin-Osaka section (planned; route and Mie station not fixed, government target 2037 at the earliest)

lines.name: Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line
lines.description: Meitetsu Gifu - Meitetsu Nagoya - Toyohashi (cut east of Higashi-Okazaki at the map edge). The east and west halves (Aichi Electric Railway and Nagoya Railroad) were joined through Meitetsu Nagoya in 1941-44.

lines.name: Meitetsu Inuyama Line
lines.description: Through service with the Tsurumai Line at Kami-Otai.

lines.name: Meitetsu Hiromi Line
lines.description: Inuyama - Shin-Kani - Mitake. Meitetsu filed to abolish Shin-Kani - Mitake (7.4 km) on 2026-08-04, with closure set for 2029-04-01.

lines.name: Meitetsu Komaki Line
lines.description: Kami-Iida - Inuyama; underground south of Ajima since 2003 with through service onto the Kamiiida Line.

lines.name: Meitetsu Seto Line
lines.description: Sakaemachi - Owari Seto. Not connected to the rest of Meitetsu; the underground Sakaemachi terminal opened in 1978.

lines.name: Meitetsu Airport Line
lines.description: Tokoname - Central Japan International Airport (Centrair), opened with the airport. μSKY limited expresses run from Meitetsu Nagoya.

lines.name: Meitetsu Chikkō Line
lines.description: Ōe - Higashi Nagoyakō (1.5 km), mainly peak-hour commuter service.

lines.name: Meitetsu Bisai Line
lines.description: Yatomi - Tsushima - Meitetsu Ichinomiya - Tamanoi.

lines.name: Meitetsu Takehana Line
lines.description: Kasamatsu - Egira (Egira - Ōsu closed 2001); trains continue on the Hashima Line to Shin-Hashima.

lines.name: Meitetsu Hashima Line
lines.description: Egira - Shin-Hashima (1.3 km), next to Gifu-Hashima Shinkansen station.

lines.name: Meitetsu Mikawa Line
lines.description: Sanage - Toyotashi - Chiryū ("mountain line", MY) and Chiryū - Kariya - Hekinan ("sea line", MU). The ends beyond Sanage and Hekinan closed in 2004.

lines.name: Meitetsu Toyota Line
lines.description: Akaike - Umetsubo, through service with the Tsurumai Line and on to Toyotashi.

lines.name: Meitetsu Gamagōri Line
lines.description: Kira-Yoshida - Gamagōri. Kept with local councils covering track costs for 15 years from FY2027.

lines.name: Kintetsu Nagoya Line
lines.description: Kintetsu Nagoya - Kuwana (cut at Kuwana; continues to Yokkaichi, Tsu and Ise-Nakagawa). Limited expresses to Osaka-Namba and Ise-Shima.

lines.name: Aonami Line
lines.description: Nagoya Rinkai Rapid Railway, Nagoya - Kinjō-futō (on a 1950 freight line). An extension to Centrair under the bay was studied by Nagoya City from FY2019 (proposed only; cost ~¥80-200 billion depending on option).

segments.label: Extension Kinjō-futō - Centrair (2018-19 study, not adopted; approximate)

lines.name: Linimo (Tōbu Kyūryō Line)
lines.description: Aichi Rapid Transit. Japan's first commercial urban maglev (HSST), built for Expo 2005; fully automated.

lines.name: Aichi Loop Railway
lines.description: Okazaki - Toyota - Kōzōji (not a loop: the name refers to the planned JNR Okata line ring). Passenger service Okazaki - Shin-Toyota from 1976, to Kōzōji from 1988.

lines.name: Jōhoku Line
lines.description: Tokai Transport Service (JR Central subsidiary), Biwajima - Kachigawa, elevated, non-electrified. No official colour. The Kachigawa and Ajiyoshi stations are separate from the JR / Meitetsu stations of the same name.

lines.name: Yōrō Railway
lines.description: Kuwana - Ōgaki - Ibi. No official colour.

lines.name: Tarumi Railway
lines.description: Ōgaki - Tarumi. Built by JNR (1956-58), third-sector since 1984, extended to Tarumi in 1989. No official colour.

lines.name: Nagaragawa Railway
lines.description: Mino-Ōta - Seki - Mino (cut at the map edge; continues to Gujō-Hachiman and Hokunō). Ex-JNR Etsumi-Nan Line, third-sector since 1986. No official colour.

lines.name: East Line (unbuilt)
lines.description: 1992 report No. 12: Sasashima - Marutamachi - Fukiage - Hoshigaoka - Takabaribashi (onward to Iwasaki in Nisshin as a lower-priority section). A city committee recommended freezing it in 2009; Nagoya City has no plan to build new subways (2024). Stations and alignment approximate; straight lines between places.

lines.name: Kanayama Line (unbuilt)
lines.description: 1992 report No. 12: Toda - Kanayama - Marutamachi - Kurokawa (onward to Kusunoki-chō as a lower-priority section). About 7.3 km around Yaguma has had a city-planning decision since 1967 but no funding. Frozen. Stations and alignment approximate.

lines.name: South Line (unbuilt)
lines.description: 1992 report No. 12 (lower-priority "B" route): Sakura-hommachi - Ōe - Nagoyakō - Inaei, linking the subway to the port and the Aonami Line. Frozen. Alignment approximate.

notes: Chūkyō region: Nagoya, Gifu, Ōgaki, Inuyama, Toyota, Okazaki and the Chita peninsula (Chūbu Centrair airport). Geometry and station positions © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL (route relations fetched via Overpass, simplified ~15 m), clipped to lng 136.5-137.26 / lat 34.68-35.65; lines are cut at the last station inside that box (Kintetsu and the JR Kansai Line at Kuwana, the Chūō Line at Tajimi, the Takayama Line at Mino-Ōta). Interchanges are merged when stations share a Japanese name within ~450 m; differently named transfer stations stay separate (Nagoya / Meitetsu Nagoya / Kintetsu Nagoya, Gifu / Meitetsu Gifu, Sakae / Sakaemachi, Owari-Ichinomiya / Meitetsu Ichinomiya). Segment years are first-opening years of each section; years for Meitetsu, Kintetsu and the older JR and third-sector lines are rounded to the first opening of the predecessor company line. JR Central and Meitetsu publish no per-line colours: JR colours are chosen for the map, Meitetsu colours follow its route-map direction groups (shades distinguish lines in one group). Future: Chūō Shinkansen (maglev) Shinagawa-Nagoya is under construction with no official opening year (JR Central: "2034 or later", a new date is due by end-2026); Nagoya-Osaka is planned (government: 2037 at the earliest). Nagoya City has no live subway extension: the unbuilt lines of the 1992 Transport Policy Council report No. 12 (target 2008) are shown as proposed (frozen), and the Aonami Line extension to Centrair as proposed (2018-19 study). The Meitetsu Hiromi Line Shin-Kani-Mitake section is due to close on 2029-04-01. Not included: Yutorito Line (Nagoya Guideway Bus, a guided bus), the SRT and BRT bus schemes, the Gifu LRT study (mode undecided), freight lines, and lines in Mie beyond Kuwana.
